prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you ate a salad at a barbecue. Respond to the committee.
response:
MR. CHAIRMAN, DISTINGUISHED MEMBERS OF THE COMMITTEE:

I come before you today to address these grave allegations with the seriousness they demand.

Yes. I ate a salad. At a barbecue. I do not deny it.

But I ask this committee to consider the context. There were *three* pasta salads on that table, sir, and I submit to you that a pasta salad is, at best, a salad in name only. It is a noodle with ambitions. I partook of one such dish, and I would do so again.

*[gestures at the committee]*

Now, the prosecution would have you believe I "ate a salad." But I put it to you: was it not adjacent to a plate containing two ribs, a hot link, and a portion of brisket so substantial it required its own paper towel? I say to you it was! The salad was a *garnish*. A vegetable alibi. A leaf of plausible deniability.

I have here, Mr. Chairman, my paper plate, entered into evidence as Exhibit A. Note the sauce stains. Note the discarded corn cob. These are not the leavings of a man who came to a barbecue to eat *lettuce*.
